tracks.narration: Stack an N type and a P type MOSFET — and you get a logic gate that wastes almost no power at rest.
V D D on top, ground on the bottom. The P type sits up high, the N type down low, and both gates are wired to the same input.
Drop V in to ground — the P type turns on, the N type turns off, and V out is pulled up to V D D. Push V in to V D D and the opposite happens; V out drops to ground.
Plot V out against V in and you get the transfer curve — flat at V D D, a sharp drop at the midpoint, then flat at zero. That sharpness is what makes the gate a clean digital element.
Only one transistor conducts at any settled input. No path from V D D to ground means almost no static current — that is why CMOS logic dominates.
